body.statement: In the categorical-instrument model with \(K\geq3\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{face}}\), and indeed any data-based random closed set, cannot simultaneously have asymptotic containment coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly along all \(n^{-1/2}\)-local sequences through intersections of optimal faces and contract in support-function or Hausdorff distance to \(Q_x^*(p_x)\) at any deterministic rate tending to zero.  More precisely, there is an admissible full-compliance local sequence through a codimension-one optimal-face intersection on which either distance is at least \(\sqrt{2}\) with probability bounded away from zero.  Hence neither uniform consistency nor uniform root-\(n\) contraction is possible without selecting a population face.  Exact confidence-fiber coverage remains valid, but any uniform vanishing-rate contraction requires excluding such intersections by a face-separation condition or weakening the target to a local outer limit.
body.proof_tex:
We give an explicit regular-submodel certificate and then derive the claimed rate-free obstruction from its fixed-error lower bound.  A procedure that is uniformly valid over \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{IV}}\) must in particular be valid on every admissible submodel constructed below.

Take one stratum \(\mathcal X=\{x\}\), take \(\mathcal Z=\mathcal A=\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), and let \(Z\) be uniform on \(\mathcal Z\).  If the support-restricted class is nonempty, Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}stratum\text{-}instrument\text{-}support}\) implies \(K\pi_{\min}\leq1\), so this design has \(\pi_{xz}=1/K\geq\pi_{\min}>0\).  For every \(\tau\in(-1/8,1/8)\), define
\[
 m_0(\tau)=\tfrac12,\qquad
 m_1(\tau)=\tfrac12+\tau,\qquad
 m_a(\tau)=\tfrac14\quad(2\leq a<K).
\]
Conditional on the degenerate value \(X=x\), draw the binary coordinates \(Y(a)\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), independently with
\[
 \Pr\{Y(a)=1\mid X=x\}=m_a(\tau),
\]
independently of \(Z\).  Set \(A(z)=z\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z\), and define \(A=A(Z)\) and \(Y=Y(A)\).  Independence of \(Z\) from the complete finite response type \(((A(z))_z,(Y(a))_a)\) verifies Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}instrument\text{-}randomization}\).  The two defining observation equations verify Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}consistency}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}exclusion}\).  The displayed joint distribution of the binary response vector induces a nonnegative vector of response-type probabilities summing to one, so it is a feasible member of every displayed response fiber and verifies Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}response\text{-}fiber\text{-}compatibility}\).  Thus the resulting observable law \(P_\tau\) belongs to \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{IV}}\).

The observable map sends this structural law to the law of \(O=(X,Z,A,Y)\) with conditional cells
\[
 p_{xzay}(\tau)
 =\mathbf 1\{a=z\}m_z(\tau)^y\{1-m_z(\tau)\}^{1-y}.
\]
The unobserved causal parameter in stratum \(x\) is
\[
 \theta_x=\bigl(E_\tau\{Y(a)\mid X=x\}\bigr)_{a\in\mathcal A}
 \in[0,1]^K.
\]
Under the maintained response-type restrictions, its identified set at the observable law is
\[
 \Theta_I(P_\tau)
 =\{Cw:w\in\mathcal W_x(p_x(\tau))\}
 =\mathcal M_x(p_x(\tau)),
\]
where the first equality is the response-type projection in Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}response\text{-}fiber}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}action\text{-}mean\text{-}polytope}\).  We next compute this identified set rather than stipulating it.

Let \(w\in\mathcal W_x(p_x(\tau))\).  Although Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}response\text{-}fiber}\) deletes one observed-cell equality for each \(z\), all deleted equalities are recovered: for any fixed \(z\), the model-implied probabilities across \((a,y)\) sum to \(\mathbf 1^\top w=1\), as do the observed cells, so the omitted equality is the difference between the two unit sums and the retained equalities.  Hence \(Bw=p_x(\tau)\).  Every observed cell with \(a\neq z\) has probability zero.  Nonnegativity of \(w\) therefore gives, for every response type \(r\),
\[
 w_r>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad a_r(z)=z
 \quad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal Z.
\]
Indeed, if \(a_r(z)\neq z\), the type contributes the strictly positive amount \(w_r\) to exactly one zero-probability off-diagonal cell at that \(z\), contradicting the corresponding equality in \(Bw=p_x(\tau)\).  For each \(a\in\mathcal A\), the equality for the observed cell \((Z,A,Y)=(a,a,1)\) now yields
\[
 (Cw)_a
 =\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r y_r(a)
 =P_\tau(Y=1\mid X=x,Z=a)
 =m_a(\tau).
\]
Thus every compatible response law has the same action-mean vector.  Conversely, the response-type distribution constructed above is feasible and has that vector.  Consequently the bound is sharp and singleton-valued:
\[
 \Theta_I(P_\tau)=\mathcal M_x(p_x(\tau))=\{m(\tau)\}.
\]
This proves the relationship between the causal parameter and the observed-law identifying functional.

We next use simplex extreme-point algebra to solve the decision problem.  For a singleton identified set, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}saddle}\) gives, for every \(q\in\Delta_K\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_x(q,p_x(\tau))
 &=\max_{b\in\mathcal A}(e_b-q)^\top m(\tau)\\
 &=\max_{b\in\mathcal A}m_b(\tau)-q^\top m(\tau).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first term is independent of \(q\), while \(q^\top m(\tau)\) is a convex combination of the coordinates of \(m(\tau)\).  It is maximized exactly by those \(q\) supported on the maximizing coordinates.  Since \(m_a(\tau)=1/4\) for \(a\geq2\), direct comparison of coordinates gives
\[
 Q_x^*(p_x(0))=\operatorname{conv}\{e_0,e_1\},
\]
\[
 Q_x^*(p_x(\tau))=\{e_1\}\quad(\tau>0),
 \qquad
 Q_x^*(p_x(\tau))=\{e_0\}\quad(\tau<0).
\]
Thus \(\tau=0\) is a codimension-one intersection of optimal faces, and perturbations of opposite signs select opposite endpoints.

Let \(\widehat S_n\) be an arbitrary data-based random closed set.  Give Hausdorff and support-function distances their extended value \(+\infty\) whenever the realized set is not nonempty and compact; such realizations cannot aid a contraction claim.  For a nonempty compact set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^K\), write \(h_S(u)=\sup_{s\in S}u^\top s\), and define the support-function distance as
\[
 d_{\mathrm{sf}}(S,T)
 =\sup_{\lVert u\rVert_2\leq1}|h_S(u)-h_T(u)|.
\]
Suppose \(\widehat S_n\) has asymptotic containment coverage at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly along all \(n^{-1/2}\)-local sequences through the preceding face intersection.  The constant sequence \(P_0\) is one such sequence, so honesty implies
\[
 P_0^n\!\left\{\operatorname{conv}\{e_0,e_1\}\subseteq\widehat S_n\right\}
 \geq1-\alpha-o(1).
\]

Fix \(c>0\) and set \(\tau_n=c/\sqrt n\).  Exactly two entries of \(p_x(\tau_n)-p_x(0)\) are nonzero, equal to \(\tau_n\) and \(-\tau_n\), so \((P_{\tau_n})_n\) is an \(n^{-1/2}\)-local sequence through \(P_0\); also \(|\tau_n|<1/8\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  With \(L_\tau=dP_\tau/dP_0\), direct division of cell probabilities gives
\[
 L_\tau=
 \begin{cases}
 1+2\tau,&(Z,A,Y)=(1,1,1),\\
 1-2\tau,&(Z,A,Y)=(1,1,0),\\
 1,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The two exceptional cells each have \(P_0\)-probability \(1/(2K)\).  Therefore
\[
 E_0(L_\tau-1)^2
 =\frac{1}{2K}(2\tau)^2+\frac{1}{2K}(-2\tau)^2
 =\frac{4\tau^2}{K}.
\]
Under Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}sampling}\), the product likelihood ratio is \(L_{\tau_n}^{(n)}=\prod_{i=1}^nL_{\tau_n}(O_i)\).  Since \(E_0L_{\tau_n}=1\), independence yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_0\!\left(L_{\tau_n}^{(n)}-1\right)^2
 &=E_0\!\left\{(L_{\tau_n}^{(n)})^2\right\}-1\\
 &=\left\{E_0(L_{\tau_n}^2)\right\}^n-1\\
 &=\left(1+\frac{4\tau_n^2}{K}\right)^n-1\\
 &\leq \exp(4c^2/K)-1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For any event \(E\), the likelihood-ratio identity and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |P_{\tau_n}^n(E)-P_0^n(E)|
 &\leq \frac12E_0|L_{\tau_n}^{(n)}-1|\\
 &\leq\frac12\left[E_0\!\left\{(L_{\tau_n}^{(n)}-1)^2\right\}\right]^{1/2}\\
 &\leq \rho_K(c):=\frac12\sqrt{\exp(4c^2/K)-1}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Because \(\rho_K(c)\to0\) as \(c\downarrow0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), choose \(c\) so that \(\rho_K(c)<1-\alpha\), and set
\[
 \delta=1-\alpha-\rho_K(c)>0.
\]
Transfer of the coverage event from \(P_0^n\) to \(P_{\tau_n}^n\) then gives
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_{\tau_n}^n\{e_0\in\widehat S_n\}
 \geq\delta>0.
\]

Under \(P_{\tau_n}\), the exact population optimizer correspondence is \(\{e_1\}\).  On the event \(e_0\in\widehat S_n\), the directed distance from \(\widehat S_n\) to \(\{e_1\}\) gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm H}(\widehat S_n,\{e_1\})
 \geq\lVert e_0-e_1\rVert_2=\sqrt2.
\]
For the support-function distance, take \(u=(e_0-e_1)/\sqrt2\).  Then \(\lVert u\rVert_2=1\), and on the same event
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_{\mathrm{sf}}(\widehat S_n,\{e_1\})
 &\geq h_{\widehat S_n}(u)-h_{\{e_1\}}(u)\\
 &\geq u^\top(e_0-e_1)=\sqrt2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Writing \(d_n\) for either distance, we have proved the fixed-error certificate
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_{\tau_n}^n\{d_n\geq\sqrt2\}\geq\delta>0.
\]

This fixed lower bound rules out every vanishing contraction rate, not only the root-\(n\) rate.  Indeed, let \((r_n)_n\) be any deterministic positive sequence with \(r_n\to0\), and fix any finite \(M>0\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(Mr_n<\sqrt2\), whence
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_{\tau_n}^n\{d_n/r_n>M\}
 \geq\delta>0.
\]
Thus \(d_n/r_n\) is not tight along this admissible local sequence, so uniform \(O_P(r_n)\) contraction is impossible for every vanishing \(r_n\).  Moreover, for every fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,\sqrt2)\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}P_{\tau_n}^n\{d_n>\epsilon\}
 \geq\delta>0,
\]
which rules out uniform consistency itself.  Taking \(r_n=n^{-1/2}\) yields the advertised root-\(n\) impossibility as a special case.  The argument treated \(\widehat S_n\) as arbitrary, so it applies in particular to sets produced by \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{face}}\), and no population face was selected.

Finally, this impossibility does not contradict exact confidence-set inversion.  The already-established Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}cp\text{-}correspondence\text{-}coverage}\) gives uniform finite-sample containment coverage for the confidence-fiber union, including at face intersections.  The fixed-error certificate shows why an honest set must be allowed to retain locally indistinguishable faces there: exact uniform validity survives, but uniform contraction to the exact optimizer correspondence at any vanishing rate does not.
